decision_conditions:
<span lang="EN-US" style="line-height: 115%;">The
proposed dwellinghouse, by reason of its siting within the curtilage of an
existing dwellinghouse would be sited on garden land. As such, the principle of
the development is at odds with the Harrow Core Strategy of directing new
residential and other development to the Harrow and Wealdstone Intensification
Area, town centres and, in suburban areas, to strategic previously developed
sites and would therefore harm its implementation contrary to the National
Planning Policy Framework 2024, policy D3 D(11) of The London Plan 2021,
policies CS1.A and CS1.B of the Harrow Core Strategy 2012 and adopted
Supplementary Planning Document: Garden Land Development (2013</span><span lang="EN-US" style="font-size:12.0pt;line-height:
115%;font-family:&quot;Aptos&quot;,sans-serif;mso-ascii-theme-font:minor-latin;
mso-fareast-font-family:Aptos;mso-fareast-theme-font:minor-latin;mso-hansi-theme-font:
minor-latin;mso-bidi-font-family:&quot;Times New Roman&quot;;mso-bidi-theme-font:minor-bidi;
mso-ansi-language:EN-US;mso-fareast-language:EN-US;mso-bidi-language:AR-SA">).</span>

<p><span style="line-height: 115%;">The proposed
detached dwellinghouse, by reason of its siting resulting to erosion of gap
between 229 The Heights and 51A Dabbs Hill Lane, would introduce a cramped and
overdeveloped appearance &nbsp;that would interrupt the pattern and grain of
development within the Dabbs Hill Lane and The Heights street scene, contrary
to the high quality design aspirations of the National Planning Policy
Framework (2024), Policies D3.D (1) and D3.D (11) of the London Plan (2021),
Policy CS1.B of the Harrow Core Strategy (2012), Policy DM1 of the Harrow
Development Management Polices Local Plan (2013) and the Residential Design
Guide Supplementary Planning Document (2010).</span></p>

<p><span style="line-height: 115%;">The proposal,
by reason of lack of surface water drainage strategy, fails demonstrate that
the proposed development would effectively manage and mitigate measures to
control the rate and volume of surface water runoff, to ensure separation of
surface and foul water systems, make provision for storage and demonstrate
arrangements for the management and maintenance of the measures used. The
proposed development would therefore be contrary to the National Planning
Policy Framework (2024), policy SI 12 of The London Plan (2021), Core Policy
CS1 U of Harrow Core Strategy (2012) policies DM10 of the Harrow Development
Management Polices Local Plan (2013).</span></p>
